classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught reflection or half-turn to each supplied branch, tracking the labelled minimum and intercept; rotation turns the minimum into a maximum.

content.prompt: Complete the following diagrams to make the graphs represent: (i) even functions, (ii) odd functions.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 40, left graph in the 40–41 row.
spec.description: The supplied branch starts at the unlabelled origin with a horizontal tangent and rises, concave upward, into quadrant I, ending in an arrow. Both axes have positive-direction arrowheads and x/y labels. No ticks, numerical labels or grid are supplied. The canvas provides blank space for the missing branch.
spec.mathematics: The graph is unscaled and has no supplied equation. Bezier control coordinates describe its visible schematic shape only; they do not assert numerical points or a function formula.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source right-hand branch is visible. The reflected branch is withheld.

answer.short: Reflect the supplied branch in the $y$-axis, adding the matching branch in quadrant II.
answer.worked:
An even function has reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis. Reflect every point $(x,y)$ of the supplied branch to $(-x,y)$.

The added branch lies in quadrant II and meets the original at the origin. Retain the supplied branch.

spec.description: Complete graph with the original right branch and its exact reflection in the y-axis. Both outer ends have arrows.
spec.mathematics: The added branch is obtained by the transformation (x,y) to (-x,y). The original branch and its horizontal tangent at the origin are preserved. No equation or scale is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution graph, visible only with answers.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 40, left graph in the 40–41 row.
spec.description: A second copy of the supplied unscaled right-hand branch, with the same axes, arrowheads and x/y labels. The lower-left quadrant is blank for completion.
spec.mathematics: The source supplies a horizontal tangent at the origin and an increasing, concave-up branch in quadrant I. Internal drawing coordinates are schematic, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original right-hand branch is visible. The rotated branch is withheld.

answer.short: Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin, adding the matching branch in quadrant III.
answer.worked:
An odd function has $180^\circ$ rotational symmetry about the origin. Rotate every point $(x,y)$ of the supplied branch to $(-x,-y)$.

The added branch lies in quadrant III and meets the original at the origin. Retain the supplied branch.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher answers, printed page 607, Exercise 2N essential problems, question 40, second sketch.
spec.description: Complete graph with the original quadrant-I branch and its exact rotation into quadrant III. Both outer ends have arrows.
spec.mathematics: The added branch is obtained by (x,y) to (-x,-y), giving rotational symmetry about the origin. No equation or numerical scale is inferred.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution graph, visible only with answers.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 41, right graph in the 40–41 row.
spec.description: The supplied branch starts at the origin, descends to the filled minimum (1,-1), rises through x=2 and continues to an arrow. Preserve the dashed guides from the minimum to both axes, the label 1 above the x-axis, 2 below/right of the intercept, and -1 left of the y-axis. No grid or origin label is supplied.
spec.mathematics: The origin, minimum (1,-1) and intercept (2,0) are source givens. Smooth Bezier segments preserve these anchors and the visible concave-up shape without asserting an unstated equation. The negative-x region remains available for the reflected branch.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied branch, minimum, guides and labels are visible. The even completion is withheld.

answer.short: Reflect in the $y$-axis. The added branch has minimum $(-1,-1)$ and passes through $(-2,0)$.
answer.worked:
For an even function, reflect each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,y)$.

The minimum $(1,-1)$ maps to $(-1,-1)$, and the intercept $(2,0)$ maps to $(-2,0)$. The origin stays fixed.

Draw the reflected branch through these points, continuing upward to the left. Retain the original right-hand branch.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher answers, printed page 607, Exercise 2N essential problems, question 41, first sketch.
spec.description: Complete even graph with minima labelled (-1,-1) and (1,-1), x-intercepts -2, 0 and 2, and upward arrows on both outer branches. The original right-hand guides and labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: The entire added branch is the exact y-axis reflection of the supplied branch. The central join at the origin preserves the source branch rather than replacing the graph with a different smooth curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution and transformed-coordinate labels, visible only with answers.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 41, right graph in the 40–41 row.

spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied curve, point, guides and labels are visible. The odd completion is withheld.

answer.short: Rotate $180^\circ$ about the origin. The added branch has maximum $(-1,1)$ and passes through $(-2,0)$.
answer.worked:
For an odd function, rotate each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,-y)$.

The minimum $(1,-1)$ maps to the maximum $(-1,1)$, and the intercept $(2,0)$ maps to $(-2,0)$. The origin stays fixed.

Draw the rotated branch through these points, continuing downward to the left. Retain the original right-hand branch.

spec.mathematics: The added branch is the exact 180-degree rotation of the supplied branch about the origin. The negative intercept label is placed above-left to clear the descending curve; its value and coordinate are unchanged.
